note: Phase 1 drawing test (2026-10-02), revised the same day after John's review. Read by tools/contact_sheet.py. Credits and licences are in ../research/play-image-plan.json. The failed Iphigenia at Aulis test stays in rejected/ and off the sheet.

drawings.name: Aeschylus · the Pythia (Eumenides)
drawings.alt: The Pythia, Apollo's priestess, fleeing in terror with her hands raised
drawings.source: Bötticher's 1859 drawing of an Apulian krater, Orestes at Delphi (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Engraved plate: cut along her own lines, with straight cuts across blank paper; Apollo's overlapping foot erased; potrace
drawings.verdict: Clean. Revised twice: arm, head curl, fingers, knee edge and the whole shawl are in. One line is drawn in: her dress's black stripe, continued 45px across the gap where Apollo's foot was erased.

drawings.name: Sophocles · Euphorbos carrying the infant Oedipus
drawings.alt: The shepherd Euphorbos carrying the infant Oedipus on his shoulder, a long spear in his hand
drawings.source: Achilles Painter neck-amphora, Cabinet des médailles 372, four photographs by ArchaiOptix (CC BY-SA 4.0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photos taken off the vase (a fitted model of the vase and cameras, flattened without shear); upper body from the close view, lower from the frontal; clay mask, lines by local contrast redrawn even; hand, faces and sandal drawn as snapped strokes; back of the neck drawn in; spear straight at full length; potrace
drawings.verdict: John, 2026-10-02, on the second round: 'You flattened it right to my eyes.' The head now matches the close photo he pointed to; the hat no longer grows out of his neck.

drawings.name: Euripides · Iphigenia (Iphigenia in Tauris)
drawings.alt: Iphigenia, priestess of Artemis, holding out a letter tablet and the temple key
drawings.source: 1849 lithograph of the Buckingham vase, Archäologische Zeitung Taf. XII (public domain)
drawings.method: Lithograph: lines by local contrast, cut along her own lines, potrace
drawings.verdict: Clean. Revised twice: forearm, key hand, chain, sandals, veil edge and the whole tablet are in. Pylades' fingertips on the tablet's far edge cannot be told apart at this scan's size.

drawings.name: Aristophanes · Mika (Women at the Thesmophoria)
drawings.alt: Mika, in a comic old woman's mask, holding out a bowl
drawings.source: Würzburg krater H 5697, photograph by ArchaiOptix (CC BY-SA 4.0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo: clay mask, fold lines by local contrast, Mnesilochus' knife cut away, potrace
drawings.verdict: Clean. Revised: the drapery folds now run their full length. The painter's own drawing is sparer than the engravings.

drawings.name: Medea · in the serpent chariot
drawings.alt: Medea in a chariot drawn by two serpents
drawings.source: Cleveland Museum of Art 1991.1, museum photograph, full-resolution TIFF (CC0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo: clay mask, disk border cut away, netted sleeves kept; lines from the full-resolution TIFF; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable. Revised twice: the face and the netted left sleeve now show, and in dark mode the goad and the gaps inside the figure carry the clay. Still the busiest drawing.

drawings.name: Oedipus Tyrannus · Oedipus at the messenger's news
drawings.alt: Oedipus, bearded, in a long embroidered robe, his hand at his beard, holding a staff
drawings.source: Sicilian calyx-krater, Syracuse, Museo Paolo Orsi 66557, photograph by Dan Diffendale (CC BY-NC-SA 2.0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo: loose cut through the glaze, hand-drawn zones for floor, plaster, shoes and head; cracks erased and the lines they broke joined across them; lines broken by wear joined; staff redrawn as a straight rod; hair and beard drawn solid, face lines evened; hand redrawn after John's trace, every finger outlined; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable. Revised after John's review: the hair and a fuller beard are solid, the face lines even, and the hand is redrawn after his trace with every finger outlined; the mended crack beside it is gone and lines broken by wear are joined. The hem and shoes are worn on the vase and stay rough.

drawings.name: Antigone · Antigone bound, before Creon
drawings.alt: Antigone, veiled, her hands bound behind her back, her head bowed
drawings.source: Darius Painter amphora, Berlin F 3240, photograph by ArchaiOptix (CC BY-SA 4.0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo taken off the vase (a fitted model, flattened without shear), made with PhotoCraft: clay mask; lines by local contrast along their centres, redrawn as clean even strokes, breaks and mends joined; hands and face from John's traces; then his corrections marked in PhotoCraft over pass 1 (veil, profile, eye, hands, belt) drawn as he drew them; potrace
drawings.verdict: Redrawn with PhotoCraft and approved by John (2026-10-10), after pass 1 and his corrections marked over it in four sittings. No outside review.

drawings.name: Philoctetes · Philoctetes on Lemnos
drawings.alt: Philoctetes alone on Lemnos, seated on a rock under a tree, his bandaged leg drawn up, his bow case beside him
drawings.source: Squat lekythos in the manner of the Eretria Painter, Met 56.171.58, photographs by Marie-Lan Nguyen (CC BY 2.5) and the Met (CC0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photos taken off the vase (a fitted model, flattened over the scene only), made with PhotoCraft: him, the rock, the bow case and the tree as one cut-out, the tree from a flat of its own joined at the trunk's base; lines along their centres at the paint's own width; hair, beard and the black top as layered brushstrokes in stepped washes, no outline round the top of the head; the rock's brushstrokes and the shadow at his foot as washes; potrace
drawings.verdict: Redrawn with PhotoCraft and approved by John (2026-10-09), after five passes and two rounds on the hair, the tree added at his ask. No outside review.

drawings.name: Oedipus at Colonus · Oedipus at the altar between his daughters
drawings.alt: Blind Oedipus, white-haired and bearded, seated at an altar with his staff, one hand raised, between his daughters Ismene and Antigone
drawings.source: Apulian calyx-krater close to the De Schulthess Painter, formerly Melbourne, Geddes collection A 5:8; the photos in Green 2003 (pp. 4, 26, 29; HathiTrust mdp.39015060089391), with Ismene's lines and borders, and those of the altar's left end and the strip below p. 26, from a photo found online (source unknown), placed on their reprint in Taplin, Pots & Plays (2007) no. 27, checked against Digital LIMC photo 8569X101 (all in copyright)
drawings.method: Red-figure photos (Green's pages and a found photo, registered to Taplin's plate), made with PhotoCraft: the cut and the hand-placed face and hand strokes kept, John's traces of the daughters kept; outline smoothed; painted lines along their centres at their own width; Oedipus' white hair a light tone with crisp dark strokes, the daughters' hair two firm tones, Ismene's headdress black with white ribs; faces drawn at twice the size; potrace
drawings.verdict: Redrawn with PhotoCraft and approved by John (2026-10-10), after three passes. No outside review.

drawings.name: Hippolytus · an Amazon fighting a hoplite
drawings.alt: An Amazon with bow and axe fighting a Greek hoplite
drawings.source: Gerhard, Auserlesene griechische Vasenbilder III (1847), Taf. CLXV, 4, 'Theseus und Antiope': a red-figure amphora formerly in the Pizzati collection, Florence (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Coloured plate, red figures on black: the black ground gives the outline; the plate's own lines by local contrast, faint lines joined along their gaps; faces from the plate's paint at its own width; neck line, bowstring and ankle strap traced through their centres; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John on the first pass (2026-10-06). The second hoplite at the right (Gerhard's Peirithoos) and the inscription are left out. Reviewed by Grok (2026-10-06), a static read of the overlays and the credits: no missed lines, none along flaws, no wrong facts. (It noted that Gerhard heads the vase 'CLXV, 3.4': fig. 3 is the amphora's shape, fig. 4 the painting drawn, so the credit keeps '4'.)

drawings.name: Andromache · Neoptolemos killing Priam
drawings.alt: Neoptolemos, sword raised, kills old Priam on the altar, the dead Astyanax across his knees
drawings.source: Furtwängler and Reichhold, Griechische Vasenmalerei I (1904), Taf. 34: Karl Reichhold's drawing of the Vivenzio hydria by the Kleophrades Painter, Naples, Museo Archeologico Nazionale 81669 (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Printed plate, black lines on grey-brown, the ground a dark halftone: the halftone gives most of the outline, cuts along the plate's own lines where figures touch; lines cleared of grain and redrawn along their centres at 0.11%, wide black solid, faint lines by a ridge filter; the faces, hands, feet, kilt and missed lines after John's traces; the blood a wash following the plate, lines black through it; traced as drawn; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John (2026-10-06) after his traces and rulings (line weight 0.11%; the blood a wash with the lines black through it). Left out: the neck band (but for the crest), the palm and the figures beyond it, the fallen Trojan under Neoptolemos' legs and the kneeling Greek. Reviewed by Grok (2026-10-06), a static read of the overlays and the credits: no missed lines, none along flaws, no wrong facts.

drawings.name: Women of Trachis · Herakles, Deianeira and Hyllos
drawings.alt: Herakles and Deianeira with their son Hyllos, between Athena and Oineus
drawings.source: Gerhard, Auserlesene griechische Vasenbilder II (1843), Taf. CXVI, 'Herakles und Hyllos': a red-figure pelike formerly in the Durand collection (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Coloured plate, red figures on black: the black ground gives the outline, cut along the plate's lines where Athena crosses the bands; lines from the plate's own paint and its thin brown lines (ridge filter), at least 1.5 px; the crest's dotted holder built as printed; traced as drawn at the plate's weight (0.104%); potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John (2026-10-07) on the third pass, after 'too blotchy' (lines from the plate's paint instead of local contrast) and the band's ornament taken out of the crest's base. Left out: the bands and the inscriptions. Reviewed by Grok (2026-10-07), a static read of the plate and drawing side by side in thirds, the overlays and the credits with Gerhard's text: no missed lines, none along flaws, no wrong facts.

drawings.name: Seven Against Thebes · Eriphyle and the chariot of Amphiaraos
drawings.alt: Eriphyle walking ahead of the four-horse chariot of Amphiaraos
drawings.source: Gerhard, Auserlesene griechische Vasenbilder II (1843), Taf. XCI, 'Eriphyle': an archaic black-figure hydria (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Black-figure plate, drawn as silhouettes (John's choice): the black solid, incisions, hatching and dots open in it (found on the plate smoothed along each stroke); the added white moved back into register; Eriphyle's feet on the plate's contour lines, joined; her face and hands on John's traces; the end of the pale band ahead of the lead horse closed with his line; a clay rim on the dark theme
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John (2026-10-07) after the style test, more detail in the eye and faces, and the feet redrawn. Left out: the shoulder picture, the band's edges, the ground line and the inscriptions. Reviewed by Grok (2026-10-07), a static read of the plate and drawing side by side in thirds, the overlays and the credits with Gerhard's text: no missed lines, none along flaws, no wrong facts. Revised the same day: Eriphyle's face and hands redrawn on John's traces (the pupil he drew cut), and the end of the pale band ahead of the lead horse closed with his line; approved by John. Not reviewed again: John reviewed it himself ('no need for grok').

drawings.name: Suppliant Women · Amymone and her father Danaus
drawings.alt: Amymone running, and her father Danaus
drawings.source: Lenormant and de Witte, Élite des monuments céramographiques III (1858), pl. XX: a Nola amphora formerly in the Durand collection, owned in 1858 by M. Paravey (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Coloured plate, red figures on black, turned upright: the black ground gives the outline; the plate's own lines by local contrast, breaks in the print joined; hair solid inside its reserved outline; Poseidon's toes cut away along her sole; the plate's own line weight (0.15%); potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John on the first pass (2026-10-07). Poseidon, who pursues her from the left, is left out. Reviewed by Grok (2026-10-07), a static read of the overlays and the credits: no missed lines, none along flaws, no wrong facts.

drawings.name: Alcestis · Apollo with the herd of Admetus
drawings.alt: Apollo with a palm and a bull
drawings.source: Lenormant and de Witte, Élite des monuments céramographiques II (1857), pl. LIV: a Campanian neck-amphora, British Museum 1867,0508.1122, formerly Blacas (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Coloured plate across two pages, scanned as one opening: levelled first (the frame's edges straightened, each page's tilt taken out, the fold widened to round the bull's forehead dots); then as Suppliant Women; faces at the paint's own width; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John (2026-10-07) after his rulings on the scan, the split into two and the fold's widening. One of a pair with alcestis-admetus: laid side by side at their places on the plate they give the whole scene. Reviewed by Grok (2026-10-07), a static read of the overlays and the credits: no missed lines, none along flaws, no wrong facts.

drawings.name: Alcestis · Admetus on horseback
drawings.alt: Admetus on horseback
drawings.source: Lenormant and de Witte, Élite des monuments céramographiques II (1857), pl. LIV: a Campanian neck-amphora, British Museum 1867,0508.1122, formerly Blacas (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: As alcestis-apollo: the scan levelled first, then the black ground gives the outline, the plate's own lines by local contrast, faces at the paint's own width; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John (2026-10-07). One of a pair with alcestis-apollo. Reviewed by Grok (2026-10-07), a static read of the overlays and the credits: no missed lines, none along flaws, no wrong facts.

drawings.name: Libation Bearers · Orestes killing Aegisthus
drawings.alt: Orestes kills Aegisthus on his throne; Clytemnestra comes at him with an axe, and Electra stands at the right
drawings.source: Gerhard, Etruskische und kampanische Vasenbilder (1843), Taf. XXIV: a red-figure stamnos by the Copenhagen Painter, from Vulci, formerly Berlin F 2184, now Moscow, Pushkin Museum (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Coloured plate, red figures on black, one leaf photographed open: levelled first (the frame's edges fitted, mapped to a rectangle); then as Suppliant Women; faint glaze lines from the blue channel, breaks in the print joined; faces and fine curls at the paint's own width; the blood a wash; John's corrections on pass 1 laid in as drawn; the plate's own line weight (0.11%); potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John on the third pass (2026-10-07), after his corrections in Photocraft and two screenshots, and chosen for the site ('this will be the plate we use for the site'). The whole frieze; the tongue band, the meander and the painted names are left out. No outside review (John: he reviewed it).

drawings.name: Trojan Women · Menelaus and Helen
drawings.alt: Menelaus dropping his sword at the sight of Helen
drawings.source: Gerhard, Auserlesene griechische Vasenbilder III (1847), Taf. CLXIX, 4: a red-figure amphora by the Altamura Painter, from Vulci, now British Museum 1837,0609.71 (E 263) (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Coloured plate, red figures on black, made with PhotoCraft: the black ground gives the outline; black borders parted from the ground along faint clay lines; the plate's lines at the paint's width, faint dotted folds drawn along fitted curves and joined; fingers found at less blur; the left woman's profile on John's line; the plate's own line weight (0.10%); potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John on the fourth pass (2026-10-08), after his marks on 26 faint lines, the hair and the mouth. The whole picture. No outside review (John: he reviewed it; the citation checked against Gerhard's text and the British Museum).

drawings.name: Acharnians · a warrior handed his spear (the type of Lamachus)
drawings.alt: An old man with white hair holds out a spear to a comic warrior in a crested helmet, seated on a stool with his round shield, his right hand raised
drawings.source: Apulian bell-krater, Würzburg H 4689, photographs by ArchaiOptix (CC BY-SA 4.0); the drawing traces only the painting and carries no licence
drawings.method: Red-figure photos taken off the vase (a fitted model of the vase and six cameras, flattened without shear), made with PhotoCraft: two figures from two photos on one flat; clay by red less blue; walls where paint meets the ground (the shield's ray, the knee strokes); stage and door cut along their lines; painted lines at their own width, flaked breaks joined, faint strokes along fitted curves; white hair and beard as strokes in a stepped grey wash, no outline; potrace
drawings.verdict: Approved by John: the warrior on the first pass, then the pair with the old man (2026-10-08), after his marks on the shield's ray, the area between the old man's legs and the hair. No outside review.

drawings.name: Clouds · A master and his slave
drawings.alt: A comic old man in a long robe, his arm stretched out, and his white-haired slave hitching up his short tunic
drawings.source: Sicilian calyx-krater, Lentini-Manfria Group, Louvre CA 7249, photograph by Marie-Lan Nguyen (CC BY 3.0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo taken off the vase (fitted to the Louvre's whole-vase photo), made with PhotoCraft: figures by the clay map, lines by local contrast along their centres, feet cut from the stage on the sandals' lines; in colour: skin clay in both themes, clothes in washes, white hair and beard in soft strokes, the edges on John's lines; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John on the third pass (2026-10-08), after he added the slave, asked for colour and drew the edges between skin, hair and clothes. No outside review (the citation checked against the Louvre's record).

drawings.name: Ajax · Ajax carrying the body of Achilles
drawings.alt: Ajax carries the armed body of Achilles; Briseis lays her hand on his helmet, the old Phoenix raises his hand, and a hoplite and an archer follow
drawings.source: Gerhard, Auserlesene griechische Vasenbilder III (1847), Taf. CCXI-CCXII, 4: a black-figure belly amphora of the Leagros Group, from Cerveteri, now Vatican, Museo Gregoriano Etrusco 16444 (NYPL copy, HathiTrust scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Coloured plate, black figures on clay, a silhouette, made with PhotoCraft: levelled from the frame; the black solid, incisions and lines along smoothed centres, hatched rims as straight strokes, the added white outlined on its printed line; John's marks laid in as drawn; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John on the fifth pass (2026-10-09), after his marks and circles; the copyist's phantom second hand left out (one hand on the vase). No outside review (the citation checked against Gerhard, the Beazley Archive and photos of the vase).

drawings.name: Lysistrata · Women carrying water jars
drawings.alt: Five women in long patterned dresses, three carrying water jars on their heads, meet at a fountain
drawings.source: Gerhard, Auserlesene griechische Vasenbilder IV (1858), Taf. CCCVIII, 2: an Attic black-figure hydria from Vulci, now Würzburg, Martin von Wagner Museum L 304 (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Coloured plate, black figures on clay, a silhouette, made with PhotoCraft: the clay gives the outline; the black solid with its incisions and the added white open; arms and hands outlined from the skin's smoothed shape; John's traces of the lowered hands laid in as drawn; every edge smoothed; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John on the fourth pass (2026-10-09), after his traces of the lowered hands. No outside review (the citation checked against Gerhard, the plate's signature, photos of the vase and the American School's Agora booklet).

drawings.name: Heracles · Herakles drawing his bow
drawings.alt: Herakles in a lion skin drawing his bow
drawings.source: Gerhard, Trinkschalen und Gefässe des Königlichen Museums zu Berlin II (1850), Taf. XXI, side B: an Attic red-figure amphora, Berlin, Antikensammlung F 2164 (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Coloured plate, red figures on black, made with PhotoCraft: the black ground gives the outline; the plate's lines traced as drawn at its own weight; the pale brown lines as a grey wash; the bowstring along its measured centres; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John on the second pass (2026-10-09), after his marks on the ear and the quiver. No outside review (the citation checked against Gerhard's text and Furtwängler 1885, no. 2164).

drawings.name: Ion · Apollo on the Delphic tripod
drawings.alt: Apollo seated on the Delphic tripod with a bowl and a bow, between the Pythia holding a jug and a girl reaching towards him
drawings.source: Lenormant and de Witte, Élite des monuments céramographiques II (1857), pl. XLVI, after Hamilton-Tischbein I, pl. XXVIII (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Coloured plate, red figures on black, printed sideways, made with PhotoCraft: turned upright and squared; the black ground gives the outline, drawn on the ground; the plate's lines at their own width; John's marks laid in; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John on the fifth pass (2026-10-09), after three rounds of his marks. No outside review (the citation checked against the Élite's text).

drawings.name: Helen · a warrior leading away a bride
drawings.alt: A bearded warrior in a cuirass, his spear reversed, leading away a woman veiled as a bride, his hand on her shoulder
drawings.source: Lenormant and de Witte, Élite des monuments céramographiques III (1858), pl. LVII B, after Gerhard, Auserlesene Vasenbilder I, Taf. XLVI, 1: an Attic red-figure belly amphora by the Painter of London 95, British Museum 1895,1031.1 (Heidelberg scan, public domain). The Élite reads Menelaus and Helen; the museum, Idas and Marpessa
drawings.method: Coloured plate, red figures on black, printed sideways, made with PhotoCraft: turned upright and squared; the black ground gives the outline, drawn on the ground; the plate's lines at their own width, the eyes and small marks at their printed width, the veil's dots kept; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John on the second pass (2026-10-10), after his marks on her fingers and the hair above her crown. No outside review (the citation checked against the Élite's and Gerhard's texts, the British Museum and the Beazley Archive).

drawings.name: Phoenician Women · Europa on the bull, and Phoenice
drawings.alt: Europa seated sideways on a leaping bull, looking back at a woman in a long cloak who stretches out her arm after them
drawings.source: Lenormant and de Witte, Élite des monuments céramographiques I (1844), pl. XXVIII: the two sides of an Attic red-figure Nolan neck-amphora by the Phiale Painter (Beazley Archive 214180), once at Suippes, now lost (Heidelberg scan, public domain). The Élite names the woman Phoenice; Beazley reads a woman fleeing
drawings.method: Coloured plate, red figures on black, printed sideways, made with PhotoCraft: turned upright and squared; the black ground gives the outline, drawn on the ground; the plate's lines at their own width, the line weight kept at pass 1's; the girdle and the band on the tail walled off as paint; John's marks laid in; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John on the fourth pass (2026-10-10), after his marks on pass 1 and his notes on the girdle, the tail and the ground under Europa's arm. No outside review (the citation checked against the Élite's text and the Beazley Archive).

drawings.name: Iphigenia at Aulis · Artemis pursuing Helen, who carries the infant Iphigenia
drawings.alt: Artemis in a patterned dress draws her bow, reaching back for an arrow from her quiver, at a woman in a long mantle who looks back at her as she flees, holding out one hand, a small child in her other arm
drawings.source: Lenormant and de Witte, Élite des monuments céramographiques II (1857), pl. XC: an Attic red-figure belly amphora by the Niobid Painter (Beazley Archive 206990), ex Canino and Laborde, last recorded in Paris in private hands (Heidelberg scan, public domain). The Élite reads Helen carrying the infant Iphigenia; Beazley, Artemis and Niobe with a child
drawings.method: Coloured plate, red figures on black, a double leaf levelled across the fold, made with PhotoCraft: the black ground gives the outline, drawn on the ground; the plate's lines at their own width, the line weight kept at pass 1's; the bands of paint on the clothes and the bracelets walled off from the ground; the bowstring drawn along its measured line; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John on the second pass (2026-10-10), after his note on the bands of paint on the clothes. No outside review (the citation checked against the Élite's text and the Beazley Archive).
